title: A finite integral model isolates a normalization prime
statement: Let $R$ be a commutative Noetherian integral domain [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring], where an integral domain is a nonzero commutative ring without zero divisors. Let $K=\operatorname{Frac}(R)$ be its field of fractions and $N\subseteq K$ its integral closure [def-weil-pbc-integral-closure]. For every prime ideal $Q\subset N$, there is an intermediate subring $R\subseteq C\subseteq N$, generated by finitely many elements as an $R$-algebra, such that, with $p=Q\cap C$, $Q$ is the unique prime of $N$ contracting to $p$. The local domain $C_p$ is Noetherian, $\dim C_p=\dim N_Q=\operatorname{ht}Q$, and $N_Q$ is the integral closure of $C_p$ in $K$. Localizations are taken at the complements of the named primes [def-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime]; dimension and height are the suprema of lengths of strict prime chains [def-weil-pbc-krull-dimension-ring].

source.place: Swanson–Huneke, Integral Closure of Ideals, Rings, and Modules. Lemma 4.8.4, printed p. 85 (PDF p. 99), including the two conclusions following In particular. No finiteness of the full normalization is asserted. Author-hosted PDF read online at https://www.math.purdue.edu/~iswanso/book/SwansonHuneke.pdf; local PDF WANTED.
